Surjeet vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:145306
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 30431 of 2023

Applicant :- Surjeet
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Babu Sharma,Ardhendu Shekhar Sharma

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ram Babu Sharma,, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned
Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
887 of 2012, under Sections 498A, 304B, 174 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Dataganj, District Budaun, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members on 21.10.2012 and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased on 4.12.2011 and after marriage applicant and his family members, tortured the deceased for want of motor cycle and buffalo and on 21.10.2012 applicant and his family members ablazed the victim for want of dowry due to which she died in hospital.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that although FIR of the present case was lodged on 21.10.2012 but applicant could not earlier appear before the court concerned only due to the reason Surjeet vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165129663/
1 that after the death of his wife, he become mentally disturbed and left the house of his Mausi and this fact has been averred by the applicant in para-16 of the affidavit.
He next submits that he surrendered before the court concerned on 23.5.2023, therefore, it cannot be said that applicant is an absconder.

5. At this stage, learned AGA submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died under abnormal circumstances due to burn injuries and applicant appear before the court concerned after 11 years and he failed to explain his conduct and as he is an absconder, therefore,
this ground alone is sufficient to reject the instant bail application.
6.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. From the perusal of the record, it appears that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died due to burn injuries within seven years of her marriageand applicant appeared before the trial court after 11 years and very casual and vague ground has been taken by the applicant for his non-appearance for more than a decade in para-16 to the affidavit.

It further appears that other co-accused persons have acquitted in the year 2018 and he could not even immediately surrendered and surrendered after five years, from the date of acquittal of other accused persons.
Therefore, on the sole ground that applicant is an absconder, in my view, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
8. Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected.

9. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 20.7.2023 Ankita  Surjeet vs State Of U.P. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165129663/
